issues.body: `reconcile_dispatch_head` validates only `object.sha` and ignores `object.type`. Consequently payloads such as `{"object":{"sha":"<40 lowercase hex>","type":"tag"}}` or even a missing `type` are accepted and published as the authoritative head. This contradicts the function and outcome contracts, which say a payload that is not a commit must fail closed. It can also make dispatch bind an object SHA that does not match the commit checked out/reported by the worker. The self-test fixtures always include `type: "commit"`, but no negative row changes or removes that field, so this trust check is currently untested.
issues.fix_hint: Require `node.get("type") == "commit"` together with the 40-hex SHA before returning. Add negative self-test rows for a valid 40-hex SHA with `type: "tag"` and with a missing/invalid type, asserting `WorkerPrError`; also exercise the outcome path to confirm such a payload defers as `malformed-head` with no mutation.
issues.title: Branch-ref reducer accepts non-commit Git objects

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The branch-ref store alignment and token split are otherwise carefully fail-closed and exercised in both stale/live directions, but the new reducer does not enforce its own key trust condition: it accepts any 40-hex Git object ID without proving that the ref resolved to a commit. That leaves a non-commit payload on the authoritative-head path and makes the advertised malformed-payload coverage incomplete.
